reason: The cited evidence does not support the key premises. E1 describes surface transformations of a perovskite oxide during OER, not controlled oxidation of a metallic alloy to form a protective skin. E2 shows that a high-entropy oxide support stabilizes single-atom Pd against sintering, but does not demonstrate formation of an oxide skin on an alloy catalyst or its passivating effect. The core mechanism and material behavior proposed are unsupported by the provided passages.
premises: Low-temperature oxidation of a multi-element alloy can form a self-assembled high-entropy oxide skin
This oxide skin passivates the surface against dealloying and sintering
The oxide skin retains accessible active sites for reactant adsorption
The treatment maintains catalytic activity and durability under transient low-temperature exhaust conditions
The treatment allows reduced platinum-group-metal loading
